biography.plain_text: Farhad Moshiri is an Iranian-born British investor based in Monaco. An accountant by training, he built his fortune through a long business association with Alisher Usmanov, earning a stake in the mining group Metalloinvest. He later became Everton’s majority shareholder, owning the English football club from 2016 until its sale in 2024.

long_biography.plain_text:
Farhad Moshiri sometimes challenged the investments he was asked to execute. He opposed Alisher Usmanov’s purchase of shares in the British steelmaker Corus but then managed the transaction. The investment was subsequently sold for more than twice its purchase cost, a return belonging to Usmanov’s holding company rather than Moshiri alone.

His community giving included matching support for families during the pandemic. Together with Bill Kenwright, he matched Everton fans’ donations of season-ticket refunds to the Blue Family initiative. Run by Everton in the Community, the programme tackled isolation through welfare calls and supplied emergency food parcels to people needing practical help.
